waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-22 re-check under AWH's high-water-edge ruling (curation doc open-apron rule). High water: Reclamation Pathfinder Reservoir allocations sheet (rev. 2016-05-19, after the 2012 spillway modification; UNT web archive capture 2016-12-24 of usbr.gov/gp/aop/resaloc/pathfinder.pdf): top of active conservation = uncontrolled spillway crest 5,852.49 ft (1,783.84 m). Frames, all rendered: Esri World_Imagery (WV02 2022-09-19, a drawdown year) at 600 m half-width (1.5 m/px), 140 m half-width over the loop's south row (0.28 m/px) and 120 m half-width over the shore west of it, each with the USGS 3DEP DEM in the same EPSG:3857 frame and its 1,783.84 m contour drawn; Esri Wayback 2011-06-22 (UC-G 0.3 m, release 25521) and 2020-06-05 (WV02, release 11475) z18 tiles. Finding the edge: the 3DEP lidar's hydro-flattened water sits at 1,782.25 m, and its 1,783.84 m contour runs along the vegetation/sand line on the 2022 frame and where the 2011 water stood (shore trees standing in water, water at the shelter fronts); the 2020 frame shows a narrow beach below the same line. Sites: the county's Rec1 catalog (tab Pathfinder Reservoir, group 'Sage (First Come, First Served)', one 'Sage Non-Reservable Sites' facility) names no sites, so the shelters are identified by position. Five 12-ft-style shelters with pads stand on the shore side of the loop road's south leg; measured shelter to the 1,783.84 m edge: westernmost (42.46826,-106.86507) ~7 m, second (42.46833,-106.86485) ~10 m, third (42.46842,-106.86458) ~14 m, all over open, unused bare ground with no road, tree screen or day use between and the pads 1.8-2.1 m above the edge on a low shore bank (a walk, not a bluff); fourth (42.46867,-106.86428) ~20 m but behind a tree clump; fifth (42.46892,-106.86396) ~28 m behind the belt of shore trees at the east end. Unsheltered pull-outs along the loop's west leg and the restroom sit 60-80 m back up the slope. In 2022 the imaged waterline was ~170-180 m from the shore row; in 2011 it was ~5-7 m. Result: lakefront at the three westernmost sheltered shore sites, with the drawdown caveat. The earlier 'sites in a sage draw back from the reservoir' read was mistaken: the loop is on the shore. --Claude
note: Natrona County campground off County Road 409 west of Pathfinder Dam, the middle of three county campgrounds on the marina side of the reservoir. Sheltered and open sites, ADA sites, restrooms. Lakefront only at the three westernmost sheltered sites on the shore row south of the loop road, on open ground at the high-water line; the shelters farther east look at the water through trees, and the open sites up the west side of the loop are set back. Water levels vary greatly: in a low year the water is 150 m or more from the shore row, and the county says it can be 1,500 feet off. --Claude
sisters: Diabase 13584 (lakeview) and Weiss 13586 (lakeview), checked on the same 2022 Esri frames with the 1,783.84 m contour, not decided. Weiss: its south-row shelters (~42.46806,-106.86074 and ~42.46797,-106.86037) stand ~12-15 m from the high-water edge over open bare ground, and the west row ~13 m with scattered trees; its p3-557 lead already said 'south-row shelters at the high-water line; drawdown rule keeps it lakeview', so the ruling very likely makes it lakefront. Diabase: the stored evidence says 'on the bench', but on the 2022 frame the shore-row sites sit ~7-20 m from the edge on the same low shore, no bench seen; the ruling likely makes it lakefront too, BUT the 2022 imagery predates the 2023 rebuild (11 sites with 40-ft concrete pads), so the new pads need placing first (the county's 'Diabase Campground Map' linked from Rec1). Both need their own re-check. Bishops Point 13583 is on a separate point, not marina side.
